The fur is dark orange, and the black **stripes** lie close together. Males have strikingly long hair on the cheeks and neck, which looks like side whiskers.

The Sumatran tiger lives only on **Sumatra**, the large island west of Borneo. It inhabits lowland rainforests, mountain forests and swamps. Important protected areas are, for example, Kerinci Seblat National Park and Gunung Leuser National Park. Its small size helps it to make its way through dense forest.

The Sumatran tiger is a **predator** and usually hunts alone at dusk or at night. It creeps up on its prey and overpowers it with a pounce. Its prey includes wild boar, sambar deer, muntjacs and tapirs. A tiger needs a large **territory** so that it finds enough prey.

After a pregnancy of about three and a half months, a female usually gives birth to two to three young. The young are blind at first and completely dependent on their mother. They stay with her for about one and a half to two years and learn to hunt in that time. The father does not help to raise them.

The Sumatran tiger is regarded as **critically endangered**. Probably only a few hundred animals are still alive in the wild. The greatest dangers are the clearing of the rainforest for plantations and poaching. Two closely related island tigers, the **Bali tiger** and the Javan tiger, already died out in the 20th century.

Tigers are the largest cats in the world. Today they live only in Asia, from Russia through India to Sumatra. Experts today often group the Sumatran tiger together with the extinct tigers of Java and Bali into one subspecies, the Sunda tiger. In European zoos, Sumatran tigers are kept in a joint **breeding programme**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group within a species that lives in a particular area and has features of its own.
The area in which a tiger lives and hunts and which it defends against other tigers.
The illegal killing of protected animals.
Cooperation between zoos so that a threatened animal species carries on living healthily.

gewusst: No two tiger coats are alike, and the stripes are as unique as a fingerprint.
Tigers like swimming and swim well, unlike many other cats.

teile.einleitung: The striped hyena is a shy hyena with light fur and dark stripes. It lives in North Africa, the Near East and India and is out and about mainly at night. Unlike the better-known spotted hyena, it usually lives alone or in small groups.
wichtigste: The striped hyena has dark stripes on light, grey to beige fur.
It weighs about 25 to 55 kilograms.
It lives in North Africa, the Near East and India.
It eats mainly carrion, but also fruit and small animals.
It is active at night and rests during the day in caves or rock crevices.
When it feels threatened, it raises the mane on its back.
It usually lives alone or in small groups, not in large clans.

abschnitte.text: The striped hyena is about 1 metre long and weighs around 25 to 55 kilograms. Its fur is light grey to beige with **dark stripes** on the body and legs. On its back it has a long **mane**, which it raises when in danger. Then it looks much bigger. Its front legs are longer than its hind legs, so the back slopes downwards towards the rear.

The striped hyena lives in North and East Africa, in the Middle East, in Central Asia and in India. It inhabits dry areas such as savannahs, steppes, semi-deserts and rocky hills. During the day it hides in **caves**, rock crevices or burrows. It needs water within reach.

The striped hyena is mainly a **scavenger**. It eats the leftovers of animals that lions, leopards or tigers have killed. With its extremely strong jaws it can even crack bones. Besides that it eats fruit, insects, eggs and small animals. Near villages it also searches through rubbish.

Striped hyenas are **nocturnal** and often cover long distances in search of food. They usually live alone or in small family groups. They are much quieter than spotted hyenas and hardly ever let the well-known laughing be heard. A female usually has two to four young, which are born blind.

Although hyenas look a little like dogs, they are more closely related to cats, civets and mongooses. There are four species of hyena: the striped hyena, the **spotted hyena**, the brown hyena and the aardwolf. The spotted hyena is the largest species and lives in large clans. The aardwolf eats almost only termites.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature classes the striped hyena as **near threatened**. It is poisoned or hunted because people think it is dangerous or blame it for damage to livestock. The decline of large predators and wild animals also takes food away from it. In some countries it is protected, and it is also kept in zoos.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that eats dead animals that it has not killed itself.
Long hair on the neck or back that an animal can raise.
A large group of animals that live and hunt together, as in the spotted hyena.
An animal that is out and about at night and sleeps during the day.

gewusst: A striped hyena can crack with its teeth bones that would break the teeth of other predators.
Hyenas are more closely related to cats than to dogs.

teile.einleitung: A mare is a grown female horse. After a pregnancy lasting almost a year, she usually gives birth to a single foal. In a herd of horses, experienced mares often play an important part.
wichtigste: A grown female horse is called a mare.
The male horse is called a stallion, and a castrated stallion a gelding.
A young horse is called a foal, and a female foal a filly.
A mare is pregnant for about eleven months.
She usually has only one foal, and twins are very rare.
An experienced lead mare often leads the herd to water and food.
In donkeys and zebras, too, the female is called a mare.

abschnitte.text: Among horses the female is called a **mare** and the male a **stallion**. If a stallion is castrated, he is called a **gelding**. A young horse is called a foal, and a young female horse a filly. From about three to four years old, a female horse counts as a mare.

Mares are ready to mate mainly in spring and summer, and they are said to be **in season**. The season returns about every three weeks. The pregnancy lasts about eleven months. In this way the foals are born the following spring, when there is enough fresh grass.

Usually the mare gives birth to a single foal, often at night. The foal is **precocial** and is already standing on its long, wobbly legs after about an hour. Soon afterwards it drinks the first milk, which contains especially important defence substances. The foal stays with its mother for several months and drinks her milk.

In wild herds of horses there is often an experienced **lead mare**. She decides when the herd moves on and where there is water and food. The stallion guards the herd and drives away strange stallions. On pastures with domestic horses, too, you can watch how a mare leads the group.

In Switzerland many Franches-Montagnes horses are bred, the best-known Swiss breed of horse. At the **National Stud** in Avenches in the canton of Vaud, breeding stallions are kept, while the mares are often kept on farms. In summer many Franches-Montagnes mares live with their foals on the pastures in the Jura. Mares are also used in riding sport and as leisure horses.

In Central Asia people drink fermented mare’s milk, which is called **kumis**. If a mare is mated with a male donkey, the result is a **mule**. Mules are strong and sure-footed and in the past were also used as pack animals in the Swiss mountains. When riding, mares are often just as reliable as geldings.

begriffe.erklaerung: A male horse that has not been castrated.
A castrated male horse, which is usually calmer than a stallion.
The time when a mare is ready to mate.
A young horse in its first year of life.
A cross between a male donkey and a female horse.

gewusst: A foal can run alongside its mother just a few hours after birth.
The pregnancy of a mare lasts almost as long as a whole year.

teile.einleitung: Chimpanzees are great apes from the forests of Africa and are among the closest relatives of humans. They are very clever, use tools and live in large groups. The researcher Jane Goodall observed their lives for decades.
wichtigste: Chimpanzees are great apes and have no tail.
They live in tropical Africa, especially in dense forests.
They like best to eat fruit, for example figs.
On the ground they mostly walk on their knuckles.
Some chimpanzees crack nuts with stones and fish for termites with sticks.
By grooming each other they show friendship.
The destruction of the forest is a great danger to them.

abschnitte.text: Chimpanzees have black fur, a bare face and large ears. Standing, they are about 1 to 1.7 metres tall, and males weigh about 40 to 60 kilograms. Like all great apes they have **no tail**. Their arms are longer than their legs, and they are very strong. With their strong arms and grasping hands and feet they can climb superbly.

Chimpanzees live in West and Central Africa and in the east as far as Uganda and Tanzania. They inhabit mainly **rainforests**, but also mountain forests and savannas with groups of trees. Every evening they build themselves a new sleeping nest of branches and leaves in the trees. On the ground they mostly walk on all fours and support themselves on their knuckles, which is called **knuckle walking**.

Chimpanzees like best to eat fruit, especially figs. In addition there are leaves, seeds, insects and sometimes meat, for example of small monkeys. Chimpanzees use **tools**: with stones they crack hard nuts, and with little sticks they fish termites out of the nest. With chewed leaves they soak up water like a sponge.

Chimpanzees live in groups of about 20 to over 100 animals. By day the group often splits into small parties. Through mutual **grooming** they show friendship and calm quarrels. A chimpanzee mother looks after her young for several years, carrying it first on her belly and later on her back.

Chimpanzees recognise themselves in the mirror and can plan. Researchers have taught some chimpanzees to use simple **hand signs**. The British researcher Jane Goodall observed from 1960 in Tanzania that chimpanzees make tools. That was a sensation at the time, because people believed that only humans could do that.

The chimpanzee is regarded as **endangered**. The greatest danger is the destruction of the forest through logging and farming. In addition, chimpanzees are hunted, and diseases threaten them. Protected areas and national parks are meant to help them. In Swiss zoos, for example in Basel Zoo, you can watch chimpanzees.

begriffe.erklaerung: Large apes without a tail: chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas and orangutans.
Walking on all fours, with the hands resting on the knuckles.
Mutual cleaning of the fur, which strengthens friendships.
An object with which you do a task more easily.

gewusst: Humans and chimpanzees share a large part of their genes, depending on how you count, about 95 to 99 per cent.
A chimpanzee is several times as strong as a human of the same weight.

teile.einleitung: In insects such as bees, wasps and hornets, a sting is a pointed weapon at the rear of the body with which they inject venom. They use it to defend themselves and their nest or to paralyse prey. A sting hurts, but is usually harmless.
wichtigste: Stings are found in hymenopterans such as bees, wasps, hornets, bumblebees and some ants.
The sting is a modified egg-laying tube, which is why only females sting.
The honeybee defends itself with its sting.
The venom of the bee is called bee venom.
The sting of the honeybee has barbs and stays stuck in the skin of mammals.
A honeybee dies after it has stung a person.
Wasps can sting several times because their sting is almost smooth.

abschnitte.text: The sting is a hollow, pointed tube at the end of the **abdomen**. Originally it was an egg-laying tube that females used to lay eggs. In bees and wasps it turned into a venom weapon over the course of evolution. That is why males, the drones, have no sting and cannot sting.

When it stings, the insect presses the sting into the skin and pumps venom into it from a **venom sac**. Bee venom contains several substances that cause pain, redness and swelling. The most important one is called melittin. The venom is meant to drive off attackers who want to plunder the beehive.

The sting of the honeybee has fine **barbs** like a harpoon. If it stings into the elastic skin of a person or another mammal, the sting stays stuck. When the bee flies away, the sting tears out of its body together with the venom sac, and it dies. When the enemy is an insect, however, it can pull the sting out again.

Wasps and hornets have an almost smooth sting and can sting several times. Bumblebees are very peaceful and only sting if you squeeze them or disturb their nest. Some **ants** also have a sting, for example the myrmicine ants. Wood ants, on the other hand, have no sting but spray formic acid.

If a bee sting is stuck in the skin, you should scrape it away quickly, for example with a fingernail. After that, **cooling** with ice or a wet cloth helps against swelling and pain. A sting becomes dangerous if you have an allergy or if it is in the mouth or throat. In that case you must call the emergency number 144 straight away. In Switzerland, a few percent of people have an allergy to bee or wasp venom.

begriffe.erklaerung: An insect group that includes bees, wasps, bumblebees and ants.
Small points that face backwards and stop something from being pulled out.
A small container in which the insect stores its venom.
An oversensitive defence reaction of the body that can be dangerous.

gewusst: A torn-off bee sting keeps pumping venom into the skin, which is why it should be removed quickly.
The queen bee has a smooth sting and uses it mainly against rival queens.
When stinging, a bee gives off a scent that calls other bees to attack and smells a little like banana.

teile.einleitung: Sexual selection is a special form of natural selection. In it, features prevail that raise the chances in the search for a mate, even if they make survival harder. That is why there are splendid peacock fans, huge deer antlers and loud frog choruses.
wichtigste: Sexual selection causes features to prevail that raise the chances of mating.
This applies even when these features make survival harder.
Examples are the peacock's fan and the stag's antlers.
Charles Darwin described sexual selection in detail in 1871.
People distinguish mate choice and competition between rivals.
Mostly the females choose, and the males court or fight.
Sexual selection explains many differences between males and females.

abschnitte.text: In **natural selection**, the animals survive that are best adapted to their environment. In **sexual selection**, by contrast, it is about who finds a mate and gets offspring. A feature can therefore prevail although it gets in the way of survival. A long peacock fan makes flying hard and attracts enemies, but pleases the females.

The English naturalist **Charles Darwin** wondered about the peacock's fan, because it is of no use for survival. In 1871 he described sexual selection in detail in his book “The Descent of Man”. For a long time his idea received little attention. Today it is an important part of evolutionary biology.

In **mate choice**, the females usually pick the best from among several males. Males court with colourful feathers, dances, song or gifts. Bowerbirds in Australia build artistic bowers and decorate them with blue objects. In a well-known experiment in Kenya, researchers lengthened the tail feathers of male widowbirds, and these males attracted more females.

In other species, the males fight each other for the females. In the rutting season in autumn, **red deer** roar loudly and test their strength with their antlers. In the Swiss Alps, ibex also clash with their horns. The winner can mate more often and passes on his features.

abschnitte.titel: Why do females choose like this?
abschnitte.text: A striking feature can show that a male is healthy and strong. Only a strong animal can afford large antlers or splendid plumage, which is called the **handicap principle**. The young then perhaps inherit these good qualities. In some species, such as seahorses or phalaropes, the roles are partly reversed and the females do the courting.

begriffe.erklaerung: Certain animals have more offspring than others and pass on their features.
The choice of a partner for reproduction, often by the female.
The mating season in deer and other hoofed animals.
The idea that a costly feature shows how strong and healthy an animal is.

gewusst: Charles Darwin is said to have remarked that the sight of a peacock's feather made him sick, because for a long time he could not explain it.
For their bowers, bowerbirds sometimes even collect plastic parts and bottle tops in their favourite colour.
The antlers of a red deer grow anew every year and are shed in late winter.

teile.einleitung: Toxoplasmosis is a disease caused by a tiny parasite called Toxoplasma gondii. It can spread through the droppings of infected cats, among other ways, but also through raw meat. For healthy people the disease is mostly harmless, but it can be dangerous for unborn babies.
wichtigste: Toxoplasmosis is caused by the single-celled parasite Toxoplasma gondii.
The parasite spreads through the droppings of infected cats, among other ways.
You can also catch it from raw or undercooked meat.
Cats are the final hosts, in which the parasite completes its life cycle.
In healthy people the disease usually causes no symptoms.
For pregnant women and their unborn child, a first infection can be dangerous.
Washing your hands and well cooked meat protect against infection.

abschnitte.text: Toxoplasmosis is an infectious disease that is caused by the single-celled **parasite** Toxoplasma gondii. The germ can infect almost all warm-blooded animals, that is, mammals and birds, and also people. Worldwide, probably about a third of all people have taken in the germ at some time. Most notice nothing, because the immune system keeps the parasite in check.

Only in cats and other members of the cat family can Toxoplasma complete its life cycle, which is why they are the **final hosts**. Cats usually become infected when they eat infected mice or birds. After that, for a few weeks they pass millions of tiny, tough resting forms, so-called **oocysts**, in their droppings. These become infectious only after one to five days and can survive in soil and sand for months.

People can become infected in several ways. This often happens through raw or undercooked **meat**, for example from pork, mutton or game, in which cysts of the parasite are found. Unwashed vegetables, garden soil or an uncleaned cat litter tray can also pass on germs. A pregnant woman can pass the parasite on to her unborn child through the placenta.

In most healthy people toxoplasmosis causes no symptoms or is like a mild flu with swollen lymph nodes. It is dangerous for people with a weakened **immune system**. If a woman is infected for the first time during pregnancy, the unborn child can be harmed in the eyes or brain. That is why there are special rules of caution for pregnant women.

The parasite was discovered in 1908 in Tunisia by the researchers Charles Nicolle and Louis Manceaux. They found it in a small rodent called a **gundi**, hence the species name gondii. The genus name Toxoplasma comes from the Greek word for a bow, because the germ is slightly curved. Only much later did people find out that cats play a key role in its life cycle.

After contact with cats, soil or raw meat, you should wash your hands thoroughly. It is best to clean the **cat litter tray** every day, because the oocysts become infectious only after a few days. You should cook meat right through and wash vegetables and salad thoroughly. When gardening, gloves protect you.

begriffe.erklaerung: A living thing that lives on or in another and harms it.
The living thing in which a parasite completes its life cycle.
A tough resting form of the parasite that is passed out in the droppings.
The body's own defence against germs.

gewusst: Mice that are infected with Toxoplasma lose their fear of the smell of cats and so are eaten more easily.
Anyone who has had toxoplasmosis once is usually protected from it for the rest of their life.
House cats that live only indoors and are not given raw meat hardly ever become infected.

teile.einleitung: Sea urchins are spiny sea animals that sit like little pincushions on the sea floor. They are related to the starfish and belong to the echinoderms. With hundreds of tiny tube feet and a special chewing apparatus, they graze on algae.
wichtigste: Sea urchins are sea animals from the group of the echinoderms.
They are related to the starfish, and also to sea cucumbers and brittle stars.
Their body sits in a firm shell of lime with movable spines.
They move about with many small tube feet.
On the underside lies the mouth with five teeth, Aristotle's lantern.
Most sea urchins eat algae, which they scrape off the bottom.
Worldwide there are about a thousand species in all seas.

abschnitte.text: Sea urchins have a mostly spherical shell of lime, which is called the **test**. On it sit movable **spines**, which protect against enemies. Like all echinoderms they are built with five rays, which you can see well on the empty shell. Depending on the species they are black, violet, red, green or brown.

Sea urchins belong to the **echinoderms**, together with starfishes, sea cucumbers, brittle stars and feather stars. All these animals have a **water vascular system**, a network of channels full of seawater. With it they move hundreds of small tube feet. Besides the round sea urchins there are flat sand dollars and heart urchins, which burrow in the sand.

On the underside lies the mouth with a chewing apparatus of five teeth. It is called **Aristotle's lantern**, because the Greek scholar described it over 2,000 years ago. With it, sea urchins scrape algae off stones. Some also eat seagrass, sponges or dead animals.

Sea urchins live in all seas, from the tidal zone to the deep sea. In the Mediterranean you often find the black **sea urchin** on rocks. If there are too many sea urchins, they eat whole kelp forests bare, and so-called **urchin barrens** arise. Enemies such as sea otters, fishes and starfishes keep their numbers in balance.

Anyone who walks barefoot over rocks on the Mediterranean should watch out for sea urchins, because the spines break off easily in the skin. Bathing shoes protect against this. In Japan, France and Italy the gonads of sea urchins are regarded as a **delicacy**. In science, sea urchin eggs helped to research fertilisation and the first steps in the development of a living thing.

begriffe.erklaerung: Sea animals with a limy skeleton and five-rayed build, for example starfishes and sea urchins.
The firm shell of lime of a sea urchin.
The chewing apparatus of the sea urchin with five teeth.
A system of channels full of water that moves the tube feet.

gewusst: Some species of sea urchin can live over a hundred years.
The teeth of a sea urchin keep growing and sharpen themselves in the process.

teile.einleitung: Pond farming means breeding and raising fish in ponds that have been made by people. The most important pond fish in central Europe is the carp, which is often bred in large numbers. The ponds are drained regularly so that the fish can be harvested.
wichtigste: Pond farming is an old form of fish farming in man-made ponds.
Carp are often bred in large numbers in special fish farms.
Many pond areas were laid out by monasteries in the Middle Ages.
In autumn the ponds are drained and the fish are caught.
A table carp needs about three years to grow big enough.
Pond landscapes are valuable habitats for birds, amphibians and insects.

abschnitte.text: In **pond farming**, fish are kept in man-made ponds that can be filled and drained. It is a form of **aquaculture**, that is, the farming of water animals. The ponds are mostly shallow, so that the water warms up quickly and plenty of food grows for the fish. Ditches and sluices allow the water level to be controlled exactly.

The most important pond fish is the **carp**, a peaceful fish that searches the mud for worms, insect larvae and small creatures. It likes warm, still water and tolerates little oxygen. Breeders have developed forms with a few large scales, such as the **mirror carp**. After about three summers a carp weighs around 1.5 to 2 kilograms and is sold as a food fish.

In the Middle Ages it was mainly **monasteries** that laid out large pond systems. On many fast days monks were not allowed to eat meat, but they were allowed fish. That is how the carp spread across the whole of central Europe. Well-known pond landscapes can still be found today in South Bohemia in the Czech Republic, in Lusatia and Franconia in Germany, and in the Waldviertel in Austria.

In autumn the water of a pond is let out slowly until the fish gather in a deep pit in front of the outlet. There the pond farmers take them out with nets and landing nets, which is called **harvesting**. In many regions this is a festival with many spectators. Afterwards the pond is filled again or left dry over the winter so that the soil can recover.

Pond landscapes offer a home to grey herons, ducks, dragonflies, frogs and rare water plants. Besides carp, the ponds are often also home to **tench**, pike and zander. In Switzerland there are only a few carp ponds, although fish ponds were also kept in monasteries in the past. Today it is mainly **trout** and char that are bred here, in farms with cold, flowing water.

begriffe.erklaerung: The farming of fish, mussels or other water animals by people.
Catching the fish when a pond is drained.
A fish that does not hunt other fish.
A bred form of the carp with only a few large scales.

gewusst: In the Czech Republic, Poland and Austria, carp is a traditional Christmas meal.
The largest pond in the Czech Republic, the Rožmberk Pond in South Bohemia, was already laid out in the 16th century.
In the wild, a carp can live for several decades.

teile.einleitung: A swarm of bees arises when a bee colony becomes too big and divides. The old queen flies off with thousands of workers and looks for a new home. For beekeepers this is an exciting but also thrilling event.
wichtigste: If a bee colony in the hive becomes too big, part of it swarms out and looks for a new home.
This departure with a queen is called swarming.
Swarming is the natural way in which bee colonies reproduce.
Usually the old queen leaves with about half of the bees.
In the old hive a young queen hatches and takes over the colony.
The swarm first gathers as a cluster on a branch.
Scout bees look for a new home and vote together.

abschnitte.text: A **swarm** is a group of honey bees that leaves its hive in order to found a new colony. It includes a queen and usually several thousand to over ten thousand workers. **Swarming** is the natural reproduction of bee colonies. In this way one colony becomes two.

In spring a colony grows quickly, and the hive becomes crowded. The bees then raise new queens in special **queen cells**. Shortly before the first young queen hatches, the old queen leaves the hive with a large part of the bees. Beforehand, the bees fill their honey stomachs as provisions for the journey.

After leaving, the swarm often gathers on a nearby branch in a **swarm cluster**. There it stays for some hours or days. Meanwhile **scout bees** fly out and look for a suitable cavity, such as a hollow tree. With a dance they show the others what they have found, until the swarm decides on one place.

Swarming season is mainly in May and June. Beekeepers check their colonies regularly in order to prevent swarms or to make a **split** in time. A hanging swarm can be carefully shaken into a box by a beekeeper and put into a new hive. In Switzerland many beekeeping associations pass on swarm catchers whom you can call if you find a swarm.

Swarming bees are usually very peaceful, because they have no home and no stores to defend. You should still keep your distance and not disturb the swarm. An old farmers' saying says that a swarm in May is worth as much as a cartload of hay. This meant that an early swarm can still collect a lot of honey.

begriffe.erklaerung: The departure of part of the bee colony with a queen.
A large comb cell in which a new queen grows up.
A bee that looks for a new nesting place.
A small new colony that the beekeeper makes from a large colony.

gewusst: A swarm decides on the best nesting place as if in a vote.
A first swarm can be followed by further, smaller swarms with young queens, called afterswarms.

teile.einleitung: Snake millipedes, in German Schnurfüsser, are long, cylindrical millipedes that belong to the diplopods. With their many legs they creep through leaf litter and soil, and when in danger they curl up into a spiral. They eat dead plants and so help to form humus.
wichtigste: Snake millipedes are diplopods with a long, cylindrical body.
They belong to the millipedes, but are not insects.
On most body rings they carry two pairs of legs.
When in danger they curl up into a spiral.
From glands on the side they can give off a foul-smelling fluid.
They eat dead leaves and rotting wood.
In Switzerland too snake millipedes are common, for example in the forest floor.

abschnitte.text: Snake millipedes have a long, round body like a cord, which is where the German name, meaning cord foot, comes from. The body is hard, shiny and often dark brown to black, sometimes with pale stripes. It consists of many rings, most of which carry two **pairs of legs**. Depending on the species they have about 30 to over 200 legs, but never a thousand. The legs are short and move in waves.

Snake millipedes are an order of the **diplopods**. The diplopods belong, together with the centipedes, to the myriapods. Myriapods are **arthropods** like insects, spiders and crustaceans. Unlike the fast, predatory centipedes, diplopods are slow plant eaters. Worldwide there are several hundred species of snake millipedes.

Snake millipedes live in damp leaf litter, under stones, in rotting wood and in the soil. They eat dead leaves, plant remains and fungal threads. Bacteria and fungi make further use of their droppings, and so fertile **humus** is formed. In this way snake millipedes are among the important decomposers in the forest and garden.

When in danger, a snake millipede curls up into a flat **spiral** and so protects its soft belly and legs. Many species have **defensive glands** on the sides. From them they give off a stinking, sometimes yellowish fluid that scares off enemies. For people it is harmless, but it can stain the skin.

In Switzerland many species occur, for example the **white-legged snake millipede** with its white legs. You find them mainly in deciduous forests, gardens and compost heaps. At night or after rain they sometimes climb up house walls. They are harmless and useful soil animals.

begriffe.erklaerung: Millipedes with two pairs of legs on most body rings.
Animals with jointed legs and a hard outer skeleton.
Fertile, dark soil made of decomposed plant remains.
A gland that gives off a stinking fluid for defence.

gewusst: Young snake millipedes have only a few pairs of legs when they hatch and gain new ones with every moult.
Some monkeys rub themselves with millipedes, because their defensive substances keep mosquitoes away.

teile.einleitung: Crane flies are insects with very long, thin legs that often look like giant mosquitoes. But do not worry: crane flies do not sting people. In autumn and spring you often see them on house walls or at the light.
wichtigste: Crane flies are true flies and are related to the mosquitoes.
They are larger than mosquitoes and have very long, thin legs.
Crane flies do not sting people and do not suck blood.
Their legs break off easily, which can help them to escape.
The larvae live in the soil, in water or in damp moss.
Adult crane flies live only a short time and eat little.
In some regions, mosquitoes are also colloquially called crane flies.

abschnitte.text: Crane flies have a slim body and very long, fragile **legs**. The large species have a wingspan of several centimetres. Like all **true flies** they have only one pair of wings. The second pair of wings is changed into small clubs, the **halteres**, which keep the balance when flying. The legs break off easily if an enemy grabs at them.

The most important difference from the **mosquito**: crane flies do not sting people. They have no piercing mouthparts at all with which they could bore through the skin. Adult crane flies, if they drink at all, drink only nectar or water. Many live only a few days and are busy mainly with reproducing.

The females lay their eggs in damp soil, in water or in moss. From them hatch grey, cylindrical larvae without legs. Because they have a tough, leathery skin, they are called **leatherjackets**. The larvae eat plant remains and roots, and some also eat grass roots in lawns and fields. There they can do damage when there are very many of them.

Crane flies and their larvae are important food for many animals. Birds such as starlings and blackbirds, bats, spiders and fishes like to eat them. The larvae help to break down dead plants in the soil. In this way crane flies are an important part of the **food chain**.

The best known species is the **marsh crane fly**, which often turns up in late summer and autumn in meadows and on house walls. The large cabbage crane fly is also common. Sometimes crane flies stray into the home and fly clumsily around the lamp. You can simply catch them with a glass and carry them outside, because they are completely harmless.

begriffe.erklaerung: Insects with only one pair of wings, such as flies, mosquitoes and crane flies.
Small clubs in place of the hindwings that keep the balance when flying.
A nickname for the larva of the crane fly.
A gnat whose females suck blood.

gewusst: Worldwide there are over 4,000 species of crane flies, and it is one of the most species-rich families of true flies.
A crane fly can carry on living without difficulty with five legs if it has lost one.

teile.einleitung: The veiltail is a bred form of the goldfish with long, soft fins and a double tail fin. When it swims, its fins flow through the water like a veil. It was bred a long time ago in China and Japan.
wichtigste: The veiltail is a bred form of the goldfish.
It has long, soft fins and a double tail fin.
Its body is short, rounded and deep.
It comes in orange, red, white, mottled and other colours.
It swims more slowly than a simple goldfish.
It needs a large aquarium with clean water.
It is not very suitable for a garden pond outdoors.

abschnitte.text: The veiltail has a short, egg-shaped body. Its **tail fin** is double and very long, often longer than the body. The dorsal fin and the anal fin are also long and soft. The colours range from orange and red through white to mottled animals. Without the fins it usually grows to about 10 to 20 centimetres long.

All goldfish descend from a wild form from East Asia that is related to the **Prussian carp**. In **China**, people began to keep gold coloured fish over 1,000 years ago. Over many generations, breeders chose fish with special features and bred from them. In this way many forms arose, including the veiltail, which became especially popular in Japan. Goldfish came to Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Because of its long fins, the veiltail swims rather slowly and leisurely. It needs a large **aquarium** with plenty of room and a good filter. Sharp stones or decorations can injure its delicate fins. Because it is slow, you should not keep it with fast, greedy fishes. Goldfish are sociable and like best to live in groups.

Goldfish are omnivores and eat flake food, pellets, water fleas, mosquito larvae and plant food. You should feed only as much as they eat in a short time. Too much food makes the water dirty. Regular **water changes** keep the fish healthy. Well cared for, goldfish can live over ten years.

In some bred forms the features are so exaggerated that the animals suffer. Very long fins can make swimming harder. This is then called **cruel breeding**. Switzerland has a strict animal welfare law that regulates the keeping of fishes and also bans cruel breeding.

begriffe.erklaerung: A form of animal that people have created through deliberate selection.
The fin at the end of the fish's body that helps with propulsion.
Breeding in which animals suffer because of exaggerated features.
The replacing of part of the aquarium water with fresh water.

gewusst: Goldfish are among the first fishes that people bred just for pleasure.
Released goldfish can regain their original grey colour in the wild and harm native fishes.

teile.einleitung: The black bean aphid is a small aphid that often sits in dense black colonies on beans. It sucks plant sap and can multiply unbelievably fast in summer. For gardeners it is a pest, and for ladybirds a feast.
wichtigste: The black bean aphid is called Aphis fabae scientifically.
It is only about two millimetres in size and matt black.
It often forms large black colonies on beans, especially at the shoot tips.
In winter it lives as an egg on the spindle tree, and in summer on beans, beets and other plants.
In summer, females without males give birth to live young.
Ants protect the aphids because they eat their sweet honeydew.
Ladybirds, lacewings and hoverfly larvae eat many bean aphids.

abschnitte.text: The **black bean aphid** is an aphid with a rounded, matt black body. It grows only about two millimetres long. Young animals often carry small white wax dots. There are forms with and without wings.

In the course of the year the bean aphid changes its plant. In winter the eggs survive on the **spindle tree**, a shrub in hedges. In spring, winged aphids fly to **summer hosts** such as field beans, garden beans, sugar beet, poppy or spinach. In autumn they return to the spindle tree and lay eggs there.

In summer there are only females, which reproduce without males. This is called **parthenogenesis**. They give birth to live young, which themselves have offspring after only about a week. When it becomes too crowded, winged animals arise that settle on new plants.

The aphids pierce the plant's conducting vessels and suck sugary sap. The surplus they excrete as sticky **honeydew**. Ants love this sap and look after the aphids like a herd. In return they drive off enemies such as ladybirds.

Heavy infestation makes leaves curl and shoot tips wither. In addition the aphids can transmit **plant viruses**, for example in sugar beet. Natural enemies such as ladybirds, lacewing larvae, hoverfly larvae and ichneumon wasps keep the aphids in check. In the garden a strong jet of water often helps, and hedges encourage **beneficial insects**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A small insect that sucks plant sap.
The change between different plants in the course of a year.
Reproduction without males.
Sticky, sugary sap that aphids excrete.
An animal that eats pests and helps people.

gewusst: A single bean aphid can have thousands of descendants in a few weeks in summer.
Sticky cars under trees are often covered with the honeydew of aphids.

teile.einleitung: A trophic cascade is a chain reaction in nature: if the number of an animal at the top of the food chain changes, it has consequences for many other animals and plants further down. The most famous example is the return of wolves to Yellowstone National Park in the USA. There it was clearly shown how whole food webs can change.
wichtigste: Trophic means that it is about feeding and feeding levels.
A cascade is a waterfall in steps, and in the same way the change works from step to step.
Predators at the top, such as wolves, affect plant eaters and so also plants.
In Yellowstone National Park, wolves were brought back in 1995 and 1996.
The wolves hunted elk, and as a result trees such as willows and aspens partly recovered.
Sea otters, sea urchins and kelp forests are also a well-known example.
How strongly a cascade works is still being studied closely by researchers.

abschnitte.text: In nature one animal eats another, which is called a **food chain**. Each step in it is called a **trophic level**: plants, plant eaters, predators. If something changes right at the top, the effect slides downwards like dominoes. This very chain reaction is called a trophic cascade.

In Yellowstone National Park, wolves had been wiped out around 1926. After that the **elk**, a large kind of deer, multiplied very strongly and ate young trees on riverbanks bare. In 1995 and 1996, wolves from Canada were brought back. The elk became fewer and avoided dangerous spots, so that willows and aspens could grow there again.

With more willows on the bank, **beavers** found more food and building material again. Their dams created ponds for fish, frogs and insects. Scavengers such as ravens, eagles and bears benefit from the leftovers of the wolves' prey. The number of coyotes also changed, because wolves pushed them out.

On the Pacific coast of North America, **sea otters** eat sea urchins. Where sea otters are missing, the sea urchins multiply and eat the huge kelp forests of brown algae bare. When the otters return, the kelp forests grow again. These forests offer a habitat to many fish.

Trophic cascades show how important large **predators** can be for healthy habitats. In Switzerland people discuss whether wolves and lynx affect the numbers of roe deer and red deer and so help the forest. Red deer and roe deer like to nibble young little trees. Experts stress, however, that nature is complicated and that not every effect is as clear as in the textbook.

begriffe.erklaerung: Many food chains linked together in one habitat.
A step in the food chain, for example plant eaters.
A predator right at the top of the food chain that has hardly any enemies.
Animals are released again where they had died out in the past.

gewusst: Even the mere fear of wolves changes where deer feed, which is called a landscape of fear.
The beavers in Yellowstone were in part also resettled by people, which makes the research even more exciting.
Fish in lakes can also set off cascades that affect how green the water is.

teile.einleitung: Tapirs are large plant eaters with a short, flexible trunk that live in the forests of Central and South America and South-East Asia. Although they look a little like pigs, they are most closely related to rhinoceroses and horses. They are regarded as “living fossils”, because their build has hardly changed for millions of years.
wichtigste: Tapirs are most closely related to rhinoceroses and horses, and all of them are odd-toed ungulates.
There are four species: the lowland tapir, the mountain tapir, Baird’s tapir and the Malayan tapir.
The name “tapir” comes from the Tupi language of South America.
Tapirs like best to live in damp forests close to water.
They are mostly active at dusk and at night and live as loners.
Young tapirs have a pattern of light stripes and spots for a few months.
Tapirs spread seeds in their droppings and are therefore important gardeners of the forest.

abschnitte.text: Tapirs have a massive body, short legs and a **very short tail**. Their nose and upper lip together form a short, flexible **trunk** with which they grasp leaves. Depending on the species, they grow 150 to 250 centimetres long and weigh over 300 kilograms. Their **skin is thick and tough** and protects them from thorns and branches in the undergrowth.

Like horses and rhinoceroses, tapirs are **odd-toed ungulates**. On the front feet they have four toes, on the hind feet three. Each toe ends in a small hoof, so that they can walk well even on soft, muddy ground. The name “tapir” comes from the **Tupi language**, which was spoken by native people in Brazil.

Three species live in the Americas: the lowland tapir in South America, the mountain tapir in the Andes and Baird’s tapir from Mexico to northern South America. The black and white **Malayan tapir** lives in South-East Asia, for example in Thailand, Malaysia and on Sumatra. All tapirs like **damp forests close to water**. They are excellent swimmers and can even dive, sometimes using the trunk like a snorkel.

Tapirs eat leaves, shoots, fruit and water plants. To take in important **minerals**, they lick at mineral-rich patches of earth, so-called salt licks. They are out and about mainly at **dusk and at night** and usually live as loners. They mark their territory with urine, and with their droppings they spread seeds all through the forest.

A female tapir is pregnant for about 13 months and usually gives birth to only one young. The young one has brown fur with light **stripes and dots**, which recalls a watermelon. This pattern camouflages it in the play of light and shade on the forest floor. After a few months it disappears, and the young animal takes on the colouring of the adults.

All four species of tapir are regarded as endangered or seriously endangered. The main reasons are the **clearing** of the forests and hunting. Because tapirs reproduce slowly, their populations recover only with difficulty. Zoos in Europe take part in breeding programmes to preserve the species.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of mammals with an odd number of toes on the hind foot, including horses, rhinoceroses and tapirs.
A lengthened, flexible nose, in the tapir together with the upper lip.
A spot with mineral-rich earth at which animals lick to take in salts.
An animal that mostly lives alone.
Seeds are carried by animals to new places, where new plants grow.

gewusst: Tapirs in a similar form have existed for many millions of years, and they even lived in Europe in the past.
Tapirs communicate with high whistles that you would hardly expect from such a big animal.
A grown tapir can flee into the water when in danger and walk along the bottom under water.

teile.einleitung: The telescope eye is a bred form of the goldfish with especially large, bulging eyes. They sit at the sides of the head like small telescopes, which is where the name comes from. The fish looks funny, but it needs a lot of consideration and care.
wichtigste: The telescope eye is a bred form of the goldfish.
Typical of it are its large, bulging eyes.
This bred form originally comes from China.
It has a roundish body and a double tail fin.
Telescope eyes swim slowly and see poorly.
Their eyes are easily injured on sharp objects.
It needs a large aquarium with cool, clean water.

abschnitte.text: The telescope eye has a short, egg-shaped body and long, often double fins. Most striking are the **telescope eyes**, which stick out of the head at the sides like small balls. It comes in orange, red, white, spotted and black. The deep black variety is called the “Black Moor” in English.

The **goldfish** is descended from a crucian carp from East Asia and was bred in China more than a thousand years ago. Breeders picked out fish with special features again and again and bred only from these. In this way forms such as the veiltail, the lionhead and the telescope eye came about over time. In Japan the telescope eye is called “Demekin”, which roughly means “goggle-eyed goldfish”.

Young telescope eyes first have quite normal eyes. Only after a few months do the eyes slowly grow outwards. The large eyes are delicate and can be hurt on stones or plants with hard edges. Telescope eyes also do not see especially well and often find their food more slowly than other fish.

Telescope eyes are **coldwater fish** and like water between about 15 and 24 degrees. They need a roomy aquarium with good filtering, because goldfish produce a lot of waste. The furnishings should be soft and without sharp edges. You should not keep them together with quick, greedy fish, because these snatch their food away.

Telescope eyes eat flakes, granules, water fleas, mosquito larvae and also some greens such as peas or lettuce. You should only feed them as much as they eat in a few minutes. With good care they can live to be over ten years old. Like all goldfish, they prefer to live in a small **group** rather than alone.

begriffe.erklaerung: A type of animal that people have created by choosing and breeding on purpose.
A fish that needs cool water without heating.
A popular ornamental fish from East Asia from which many bred forms are descended.
A tail fin that is split into two halves.

gewusst: Telescope eyes are born with normal eyes, and the bulging eyes grow only later.
The black telescope eyes can change colour during their lives and turn bronze or orange.
Because they swim slowly, telescope eyes are not very suitable for a garden pond with fast fish.

teile.einleitung: Remoras, in German Schiffshalter, are sea fishes that attach themselves with a sucker disc on the head to sharks, whales, turtles and even ships. In this way they let themselves be carried comfortably through the sea. The German name, which means ship holder, comes from the old legend that they could hold whole ships fast.
wichtigste: Remoras are fishes that live in warm seas all over the world.
On the head they carry a sucker disc that developed from the dorsal fin.
With it they attach themselves to sharks, rays, whales, sea turtles or ships.
Often they also swim close beside a shark and eat leftovers.
They do not harm the shark in doing so.
Some remoras also eat skin parasites of their host.
Most species grow to about 30 to 90 centimetres long.

abschnitte.text: Remoras have a long, slim body and a flat head. Their special feature is the oval **sucker disc** on top of the head. It developed from the front dorsal fin and consists of many plates lying crosswise. When the fish raises the plates, a vacuum is created, and it holds on like a suction cup. By swimming forwards it can let go again.

Remoras live in tropical and warm seas all over the world, for example in the Atlantic, the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. They also occur in the Mediterranean. Mostly they stay in the open sea, where their large **hosts** travel. There are about eight species that belong to the remora family.

Remoras let sharks, manta rays, whales and sea turtles take them along. In this way they save energy and are protected from some enemies. They eat leftovers from their host's prey and small **parasites** from its skin. The shark has no disadvantage from this, and sometimes even an advantage. Such a relationship, in which one benefits and the other is not harmed, is called **commensalism**.

Remoras eat mainly leftovers that remain when their host eats. They also snap at small fishes and little crustaceans in the water. Some species also eat skin pests such as small copepods from their hosts. In this way they clean their large companion a little.

Even the ancient Romans told that a small fish could stop a ship. That is where the German name comes from. In some coastal areas, fishermen used to tie remoras to a line in order to catch **sea turtles** with them. The fish attached itself to the turtle, and the fishermen could pull both to the boat.

begriffe.erklaerung: An organ on the head with which the fish sucks itself fast.
The large animal to which another animal holds on or from which it lives.
A way of living together in which one benefits and the other has neither advantage nor harm.
A living thing that lives on or in another and harms it.

gewusst: A remora holds on so firmly that you can hardly pull it off without hurting it.
Engineers study the sucker disc in order to build new adhesion systems for robots.

teile.einleitung: In some animals it is not the genes that decide whether a male or a female hatches from an egg, but the warmth in the nest. This is called temperature dependent sex determination. It occurs mainly in turtles, crocodiles and some lizards.
wichtigste: In some reptiles the temperature in the nest decides the sex of the young.
In the European pond turtle, the nest temperature decides whether males or females hatch.
In many turtles more females arise when it is warm.
In mammals and birds, on the other hand, the chromosomes decide the sex.
What matters most is usually the middle third of the incubation period.
Climate change can shift the ratio of males to females.

abschnitte.text: In humans, dogs or birds the sex is already settled at fertilisation, because it depends on the **sex chromosomes**. In many reptiles it is different. Here the sex is fixed only during development in the egg. The deciding factor is the **incubation temperature**, that is, how warm the ground around the eggs is.

In most turtles, females hatch from warm eggs and males from cooler eggs. This is also true of the **European pond turtle**. In many species the threshold temperature lies roughly between 28 and 30 degrees Celsius. At exactly this temperature about equal numbers of males and females hatch.

In all crocodiles, too, the sex depends on the temperature. In them, mostly males hatch at medium temperatures and rather females at very cool or very warm ones. In the tuatara from New Zealand it is the other way round from turtles, and there warm eggs give rise rather to males. In some lizards such as the leopard gecko, temperature also plays a part.

The warmth influences certain genes and **hormones** in the embryo. Depending on the temperature, more female or male hormones are made, and the gonads develop into ovaries or testes. A short, sensitive phase in the middle of the incubation period is especially important here. This phenomenon was discovered in 1966 by the French researcher Madeleine Charnier in an African agama lizard.

When beaches and nesting sites get warmer and warmer, almost only females now hatch in many sea turtles. In green turtles in the north of Australia, researchers found that almost all the young animals are female there. Protection programmes therefore sometimes move eggs to shadier places or build shade over the nests. In Switzerland pond turtles are being resettled in a few places, and there too people pay attention to the nest temperature.

begriffe.erklaerung: The process that decides whether a living thing becomes male or female.
Tiny carriers of genetic information in every cell.
The warmth at which the eggs develop.
A living thing at a very early stage of development, for example in the egg.

gewusst: Even a difference of one or two degrees can decide whether a nest produces almost only males or almost only females.
Eggs at the top of the nest are often warmer than those at the bottom, so both sexes can hatch from the same clutch.
In crocodiles, both very cool and very warm nests produce mainly females.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Kynological Society, SKG for short, is the largest umbrella organisation for dogs in Switzerland. It looks after dog breeding, shows, training and the welfare of dogs. Kynology is the technical word for the study of dogs.
wichtigste: SKG stands for Schweizerische Kynologische Gesellschaft, the Swiss Kynological Society.
It was founded in 1883 and is therefore very old.
Kynology means the study of dogs and comes from the Greek word for dog.
The SKG keeps the Swiss Dog Stud Book for pedigree dogs.
It is a member of the world federation of dog breeding, the FCI.
Many breed clubs and dog sport clubs belong to the SKG.
It campaigns especially for the Swiss dog breeds such as the Swiss mountain dogs.

abschnitte.text: The **SKG** is an association in which many dog clubs from all over Switzerland are joined together. It was founded in 1883 and has its seat in Bern. The term **kynology** means the study of dogs, from the Greek word kyon for dog. The SKG represents the interests of dog owners towards the authorities and the public.

The SKG keeps the **Swiss Dog Stud Book**, SHSB for short. In it, pedigree dogs are entered with their parents and ancestors. A dog with SKG papers has a **pedigree certificate** that proves its origin. The breed clubs lay down rules so that the dogs stay healthy and typical of their breed.

The SKG is a member of the **FCI**, the Fédération Cynologique Internationale. This world federation lays down how each breed should look, the so-called **breed standard**. For the Swiss breeds, Switzerland is the country of origin. They include the St Bernard, the four Swiss mountain dogs and the Swiss hounds.

The SKG and its clubs organise **dog shows** at which judges assess the dogs. There are also tests and competitions in dog sport, for example agility, obedience or tracking. Rescue dogs, avalanche dogs and medical dogs are also trained in clubs. Many dog schools work according to the principles of the SKG.

Anyone who wants a dog should first find out well how much time, space and money it needs. In Switzerland every dog must be marked with a **microchip** and registered in the AMICUS database. Many cantons also require you to pay a dog tax. Courses at a dog school help people and dogs to live well together.

begriffe.erklaerung: The study and knowledge of dogs.
A register in which pedigree dogs are entered with their ancestors.
A document that shows the parents and grandparents of a dog.
The exact description of how a dog breed should look and behave.

gewusst: The SKG is among the oldest kynological associations in the world.
The St Bernard is the national dog of Switzerland and became famous through rescues at the Great St Bernard Pass.

teile.einleitung: A bull is a grown, uncastrated male of the cattle family. He is the father of the calves and is usually clearly bigger and stronger than a cow. Bulls are impressive animals, but you have to be careful when dealing with them.
wichtigste: The male of the cow is called a bull.
A castrated male of the cattle family is called an ox.
Big bulls can weigh over 1000 kilograms.
Bulls are used for breeding cattle.
Many bulls wear a nose ring so that they can be led more easily.
The ancestor of our domestic cattle is the extinct aurochs.
The coat of arms of the canton of Uri shows a bull’s head.

abschnitte.text: Among cattle the female is called a **cow**, the young a **calf** and the grown male a **bull**. If a male is castrated, it is called an **ox**. Oxen are calmer and in the past were harnessed as draught animals in front of carts and ploughs. A young male that is not yet fully grown is called a young bull.

Bulls have a strong neck, broad shoulders and a massive head. Depending on the breed, they weigh about 800 to over 1200 kilograms. That often makes them almost twice as heavy as cows of the same breed. Many breeds have horns, but there are also hornless cattle.

A **breeding bull** is meant to pass on his good qualities to the calves, such as plenty of milk or good meat. Today most cows in Switzerland are no longer covered directly by the bull but by **artificial insemination**. In this way a single bull can become the father of very many calves. Well-known Swiss breeds of cattle are the Brown Swiss, the Simmental and the Eringer.

Bulls can be unpredictable and dangerous, especially when they are protecting their herd. That is why many wear a **nose ring** by which they can be led. On hiking trails through pastures you should keep your distance and not startle the animals. By the way, it is not the colour red that annoys a bull but the movement, because cattle can hardly tell red from green.

All domestic cattle descend from the wild **aurochs**. It once lived in Europe, Asia and North Africa and was much bigger than today’s cattle. The last aurochs died in 1627 in a forest in Poland. People tamed cattle as long as about 10 000 years ago.

The coat of arms of the canton of **Uri** shows the black head of a bull with a nose ring, the so-called Uri bull. The star sign Taurus is also named after this animal. At cattle shows in Switzerland, especially beautiful bulls and cows are given prizes. In some countries there are bullfights, which, however, are controversial and are banned in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A castrated male of the cattle family, which is calmer than a bull.
A young animal of the cattle family in its first year of life.
A method in which the seed of a bull is brought to the cow without mating.
The extinct wild cattle from which all domestic cattle descend.

gewusst: A bull does not see red as a bright colour, and in a bullfight he reacts to the waving of the cloth.
Through artificial insemination, a single breeding bull can become the father of tens of thousands of calves.

teile.einleitung: The siamang is the largest gibbon in the world and a true singer of the rainforest. With its inflatable throat sac it calls so loudly that you can hear it for kilometres. It lives high up in the trees on Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula.
wichtigste: The siamang is the largest species of gibbon.
It lives on the Indonesian island of Sumatra and on the Malay Peninsula.
Its inflatable throat sac amplifies its calls.
Siamangs swing with their long arms from branch to branch.
They live in small family groups with a lasting pair.
Male and female sing loud duets together.
The species is endangered, because its rainforest is being cleared.

abschnitte.text: The siamang has dense, entirely black fur and no tail, because gibbons are **apes**. It weighs about 10 to 12 kilograms and is thus the largest gibbon. Its arms are very long, and with arms outstretched it measures up to about 1.5 metres. On the neck it has a bare **throat sac**, which it can inflate like a balloon. Its scientific name Symphalangus syndactylus points to the fact that two of its toes are grown together.

Siamangs live in the **rainforests** of Sumatra in Indonesia and on the Malay Peninsula. They occur from the lowlands up into the mountains. They spend almost their whole life high up in the treetops. They hardly ever come to the ground.

Siamangs are famous for their loud **duets**. Male and female usually sing together in the morning, with their calls taking turns. The inflated throat sac amplifies the sounds like a loudspeaker, so that you can hear them several kilometres away. With the song they show other groups that the **territory** is taken, and strengthen the bond of the pair.

Siamangs eat mainly **leaves** and fruit, especially figs, along with flowers and sometimes insects. They move about by **brachiation**, so they swing on their arms from branch to branch. In doing so they can fly several metres through the air. On branches they sometimes walk upright and hold their arms up for balance.

Siamangs live in small **family groups**: an adult pair and its young. The female has a single young about every two to three years. In siamangs, the father often looks after the young as soon as it is about a year old. The species is regarded as endangered, because the rainforest is being cleared for plantations, for example for palm oil.

begriffe.erklaerung: A small ape from South-East Asia with very long arms.
A pouch of skin on the neck that can be inflated and amplifies sounds.
Singing by two voices that sing together or in turn.
Movement in which an animal swings from branch to branch with its arms.

gewusst: The call of a siamang is among the loudest calls of all land mammals.
Siamangs have no tail, because they belong to the apes.
In siamangs it is often the father who carries the young around.

teile.einleitung: The thermocline is a layer of water in lakes and seas in which the temperature suddenly falls sharply with depth. In summer it separates the warm surface water from the cold deep water. For fishes such as whitefish, it is an important boundary in their habitat.
wichtigste: In the thermocline the water temperature falls by several degrees over a few metres.
It forms in summer, when the sun warms the top layer of water.
Above the thermocline lies warm water, and below it cold water.
Water is heaviest at about 4 degrees Celsius, which is why it is almost always that cold at the bottom of deep lakes.
In autumn the surface cools, and the water of the lake mixes again.
In summer, whitefish often stay in the cooler, deeper layers of water.
The technical word for the thermocline is metalimnion.

abschnitte.text: In a deep lake the water is not equally warm everywhere in summer. At the top it can be over 20 degrees, while right at the bottom it stays at about 4 to 6 degrees. In between lies a zone in which the temperature falls very quickly over a few metres. This zone is called the **thermocline**, in German Sprungschicht, meaning jump layer, because the temperature there literally jumps downwards.

Experts divide a layered lake into three storeys. At the very top lies the warm **epilimnion**, which is mixed by the wind. In the middle follows the metalimnion, that is, the thermocline. At the very bottom lies the cold, dark hypolimnion, which in summer has hardly any contact with the air.

abschnitte.titel: Why does the water not mix?
abschnitte.text: Warm water is lighter than cold water and therefore floats on top. Water is heaviest at about **4 degrees Celsius**, so such water collects at the bottom of the lake. The thermocline acts like an invisible lid that the wind cannot break through in summer. Only in autumn, when the surface cools, does the water at the top become heavier and sink, so that the whole lake mixes.

Many fishes choose the depth of water whose temperature suits them best. **Whitefish** are cold-loving fishes and in summer often stay in the cooler, deeper layers of water. Professional fishers on Swiss lakes therefore set their nets deeper in summer than in winter. Below the thermocline, however, **oxygen** can become scarce in nutrient-rich lakes.

In deep lakes such as Lake Zurich, Lake Geneva or Lake Constance, a clear thermocline forms every summer. Divers feel it well, because when they dive down it suddenly becomes much colder. In autumn and winter the lakes mix, which brings oxygen into the depths. Because of **climate change**, the layering lasts longer today, and some lakes no longer mix completely every year.

begriffe.erklaerung: The layer in which the temperature falls quickly.
The warm, upper layer of water of a lake in summer.
The cold, lower layer of water of a lake.
When warm and cold water of a lake mix in autumn or spring.

gewusst: There are also thermoclines in the sea, and submarines can hide beneath them because they deflect sound waves.
Anyone diving in a lake in summer can feel the jump in temperature in the feet before the head notices it.
Ice floats on the lake because frozen water is lighter than liquid water.

teile.einleitung: A pest is a living thing that harms people, for example by eating crops, stores, wood or clothes. Typical pests in the garden are aphids. Whether an animal is a pest, however, always depends on the human point of view.
wichtigste: Pests are animals, fungi or other living things that damage crops, stores or objects.
Aphids suck plant sap, harm crops and weaken them.
Further examples are the Colorado beetle, the bark beetle, clothes moths and rats.
In nature every living thing has its place, and pest is a term from the human point of view.
Beneficial insects such as ladybirds eat pests.
Introduced species such as the Japanese beetle must be reported in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: A **pest** is a living thing that damages plants, animals, stores or materials belonging to people. Mostly they are insects, but also snails, mice, rats or fungi. The term comes from the human point of view. In nature, pests are also food for other animals and have their role.

abschnitte.titel: Pests in the garden and field
abschnitte.text: **Aphids** pierce plants and suck the sweet sap, so the plant becomes weak and the leaves curl up. Snails eat lettuce, and the Colorado beetle strips potato leaves bare. White grubs, the larvae of the cockchafer, eat roots. The spotted wing drosophila, in Switzerland since 2011, lays its eggs in ripe cherries and grapes.

abschnitte.titel: Pests in the house and forest
abschnitte.text: In the house, **clothes moths** eat holes in woollen jumpers, and pantry moths infest stores. Rats and mice nibble at food and can transmit diseases. In the forest, the **bark beetle** can destroy whole stands of spruce after storms or in dry summers. Woodworm, the larvae of certain beetles, eat away old wood.

Many pests have **beneficial insects** as enemies. A ladybird and its larvae eat many hundreds of aphids. Lacewings, parasitic wasps, birds and hedgehogs also help the gardener. Anyone who offers beneficial insects shelter, for example with hedges or insect hotels, needs less poison.

Farmers and gardeners protect their plants with **plant protection products**, nets, traps or with beneficial insects. In biological pest control, natural enemies are used on purpose. In Switzerland, dangerous introduced species such as the Japanese beetle must be reported to the authorities. It is important to use only as much poison as necessary, so that bees and other animals are not harmed.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that helps people, for example by eating pests.
A substance that protects plants from pests and diseases.
The thick, white larva of the cockchafer and related beetles.
Brought by people from another part of the world.

gewusst: Aphids can reproduce without males and give birth to live young that can already be pregnant themselves.
Ants protect aphids and “milk” them, because they like the sweet honeydew.

teile.einleitung: A surfactant is a substance that lowers the surface tension of water. Soap, washing-up liquid and washing powder contain surfactants so that they can dissolve grease and dirt. For animals such as the pond skater, however, a surfactant in the water can become a problem.
wichtigste: Surfactants lower the surface tension of water.
Soap is the oldest known surfactant.
A surfactant particle has a water-loving head and a grease-loving tail.
That is how surfactants can dissolve grease and dirt in water.
Pond skaters cannot walk on soapy water, because the soap weakens the surface tension.
Our lungs also make a natural surfactant.
Surfactants in waste water have to be biodegradable.

abschnitte.text: The German word, Tensid, comes from the Latin “tensio”, which means tension. A surfactant is a substance that gathers at the boundary between water and air or between water and grease. There it weakens the **surface tension**. Typical surfactants are found in soap, shampoo, washing-up liquid and laundry detergent.

Every surfactant particle has two ends. The **water-loving head** points towards the water, while the grease-loving tail hides in the grease or sticks out into the air. When washing, many particles surround a tiny droplet of grease and form small balls called **micelles**. That way the grease can be rinsed away with the water.

Pond skaters are insects that dart about on ponds and calm streams. Their legs carry fine, water-repellent hairs and spread their weight over the surface of the water. The surface tension acts like a thin, elastic skin. If you add soap to the water, this skin gets weaker, and the pond skater sinks in.

As long as 4000 years ago, the Sumerians in Mesopotamia made soap-like substances from fat and plant ash. Soap is made when fat is boiled with a lye, which is called **saponification**. In the 20th century, man-made surfactants were added, which also wash well in hard, chalky water. Today they are in almost every cleaning product.

Living things also make surfactants. In the air sacs of our lungs, a substance called **surfactant** makes sure that the tiny sacs do not stick together when we breathe out. Babies born very early often still have too little of it and therefore get help with breathing. The bile in our gut acts in a similar way and helps to digest fat from our food.

If many surfactants get into streams and lakes, they can harm fish, insects and other water animals. In Switzerland and in the EU, surfactants in detergents therefore have to break down easily. Waste water flows to the sewage works, where bacteria break the substances down. That is why you should not wash cars on the street and never pour washing-up water into a rain drain or into a stream.

begriffe.erklaerung: The force that holds the surface of water together like a thin skin.
A tiny ball made of many surfactant particles that encloses grease.
Making soap from fat and lye.
Can be broken down into harmless substances by bacteria and other living things.

gewusst: If you carefully lay a paper clip on water, it floats, but a drop of washing-up liquid makes it sink at once.
Soap bubbles exist only thanks to surfactants, and with pure water they burst at once.
Without the surfactant in the lungs, we would have to use much more effort with every breath.

teile.einleitung: The stone marten is a slender predator with greyish-brown fur that very much likes to live near people. It lives in attics, barns and sheds. It is known above all because it sometimes gnaws at cables in car engines.
wichtigste: The stone marten belongs to the marten family, like the badger and the weasel.
Its body is about 45 centimetres long without the tail.
It has greyish-brown fur and a white, forked patch on its throat.
In Switzerland it particularly likes to live in settlements, barns and attics.
It is active at night and eats almost anything, from mice to fruit.
The young are born blind and naked and are raised by the mother alone.
Many people regard it as a pest, but it also eats mice and rats.

abschnitte.text: The stone marten is about 45 centimetres long without the tail, and a bushy tail of about 25 centimetres is added to that. It usually weighs 1 to 2 kilograms. Its fur is **greyish brown**, and on its throat it has a white patch that forks downwards towards the front legs. In the closely related **pine marten** this throat patch is yellowish and rather rounded. Each paw has **five toes** with claws, with which it climbs superbly.

Stone martens live all over Europe and in parts of Asia. Originally they lived in rocky areas, hence the name. Today they are true **followers of human settlement** and live in villages and towns. In Switzerland they can be found in barns, woodpiles, garages and attics, from the Central Plateau up to the mountain villages.

The stone marten is an **omnivore**. It hunts mice, rats and birds and likes to eat eggs. In summer and autumn, cherries, plums, berries and insects are also on the menu. If it gets into a hen house, it can kill many hens, because the fluttering animals keep setting off its hunting instinct.

Mating takes place in summer, and at night you can hear cackling and screaming sounds. After that the embryo rests for several months, which is called **delayed implantation**. Only in spring, usually in March or April, are two to four young born. They are blind and naked, and only the female looks after them. After about five weeks they open their eyes.

In winter, stone martens sometimes look for a warm engine compartment, because the engine still gives off warmth after a drive. If a marten smells the scent of another marten there, it becomes furious and bites into cables and hoses. In this way it defends its **territory**. Such marten damage can be expensive. An engine wash that removes the scent and special deterrent devices can help.

Many people experience the stone marten as an annoying **pest**, because it thumps about in the attic at night and tears up insulation material. At the same time it is useful, because it eats many mice and rats. In Switzerland the stone marten is common and not endangered. It may be hunted during the hunting season.

begriffe.erklaerung: A wild animal that likes to live near people because it finds food and hiding places there.
A pause in the development of the embryo that moves the birth to spring.
The area that an animal claims for itself and defends against others of its kind.
The light patch on the neck and chest by which species of marten can be told apart.

gewusst: Although mating already takes place in summer, the young are only born around eight to nine months later.
A stone marten can slip through openings that are hardly bigger than a hen’s egg.

teile.einleitung: The tracheal system is the breathing system of insects. It consists of a network of fine little air tubes that run through the whole body and carry oxygen straight to the organs. Cockchafers, dung beetles and bees all breathe through tracheae.
wichtigste: Insects breathe with a tracheal system instead of lungs.
Cockchafers and dung beetles breathe through tracheae, fine little air tubes in the body.
The blood of insects carries hardly any oxygen.
Many insects actively pump air through their tracheae.
Flying insects often have extra air sacs.
The tracheal system limits how big insects can grow.
Marcello Malpighi described the tracheal system in the 17th century.

abschnitte.text: The tracheal system is a network of fine **little air tubes** that runs through the whole insect body. It begins at the breathing openings on the sides of the body and branches out as far as the individual cells. In this way oxygen gets directly to where it is needed. At the same time, carbon dioxide is carried out along the same route.

In small insects it is enough if the air spreads through the little tubes by itself, which is called **diffusion**. Larger insects move their abdomen like a bellows and so pump air in and out. Before taking off, the cockchafer visibly pumps with its abdomen several times to take on enough oxygen. Bees and other good fliers also have **air sacs**, which store air like small balloons.

In people, the blood carries oxygen from the lungs into the body. The blood of insects, the **haemolymph**, on the other hand, carries hardly any oxygen, because the tracheae do that job. That is why insect blood is mostly colourless, greenish or yellowish and not red. The heart of insects is a simple tube on the back.

abschnitte.titel: Limits and giants of prehistoric times
abschnitte.text: Because air moves forward only slowly through long tubes, insects cannot grow as big as they like. In the **Carboniferous**, about 300 million years ago, the air contained more oxygen than today. At that time there lived giant relatives of dragonflies such as Meganeura, with a wingspan of around 70 centimetres. Today the largest beetles, such as the goliath beetle, are only about as big as a hand.

The Italian researcher Marcello Malpighi examined the silkworm under the microscope in the 17th century and in doing so described the tracheae. Tracheal systems are found not only in insects but also in myriapods and some arachnids. Many spiders have **book lungs** as well as tracheae. Researchers think that tracheal systems arose several times independently in the course of evolution.

begriffe.erklaerung: The way a substance, for example air, spreads out by itself from places where there is a lot of it to places where there is little.
The blood of insects.
A widening of the tracheae that stores air.
A breathing organ of spiders with many thin leaves like the pages of a book.

gewusst: The pumping of the cockchafer before take-off is called “counting” in everyday German.
Some water insects carry an air bubble with them like a diving cylinder.
The larvae of dragonflies and mayflies breathe under water with tracheal gills.

teile.einleitung: The mallard is the most common and best-known duck in Switzerland. You can meet it on almost every lake, river and pond, even in the middle of town. The male with his shiny green head is easy to recognise.
